subtopic: Mizo education and written-language chronology (PYQ review)
primer: Keep the early milestones distinct: the British military school for sepoy children is reported in 1893; missionaries J.H. Lorrain and F.W. Savidge arrived in January 1894 and began a school for Mizo pupils that April; Mizo Zir Tir Bu, the early Mizo primer, appeared in 1895. Questions that say only “first school” are ambiguous unless they specify the audience or school type.
analogy: Treat these as three different milestones: a school for military families, a school for local pupils, and a printed textbook. Similar dates do not make them the same event.
traps: Do not force 1894 into a question whose options stop at 1893; first identify whether it means the sepoy school or the missionary school.
Do not confuse arrival of missionaries (January 1894), opening of the school (April 1894), and publication of the primer (1895).
formulae: PYQ anchor: Inspector of Taxes 2016, GS-III Q49 — ambiguous stem, withheld from scoring.
Chronology: military school 1893 (sepoy children) → missionary school 1894 (Mizo pupils) → primer 1895.

subtopic: Mizoram administrative history: dates and source conflicts (PYQ review)
primer: Learn the broad constitutional sequence first: the Lushai Hills District Council emerged in 1952; Mizoram became a Union Territory in 1972; statehood followed on 20 February 1987. For exact-day questions, distinguish the Council’s election, inauguration, first session and commencement of administration; sources sometimes attach different dates to these separate events. Likewise, the 2006 Gazette order formally split the Excise and Taxation Departments, while the Taxation Department RTI manual describes a separate-department status from July 1988. When official sources conflict, retain the source wording and do not treat a guessed option as certain.
analogy: An institution can be elected, inaugurated, hold its first session, and begin daily work on four separate dates—like a school being approved, opened, holding its first class, and starting regular operations.
traps: Do not substitute the first session date for inauguration.
Do not collapse a later Gazette reorganisation into an earlier administrative-history statement.
A date absent from all choices is a defective item, not permission to select the nearest date.
formulae: PYQ anchors: Excise Inspector 2019 GS-III Q73 (date mismatch); Inspector of Taxes 2016 GS-III Q73 (1988/2006 source conflict).
Constitutional milestones: 1952 Council → 1972 Union Territory → 20 February 1987 statehood.

subtopic: Mizo Peace Accord and the 1986 agreement dates (PYQ review)
primer: The Mizo Accord, formally the Memorandum of Settlement between the Government of India and the Mizo National Front, was signed on 30 June 1986. A separate Congress (I)–MNF agreement was signed on 25 June 1986, five days earlier. The peace settlement helped end the insurgency and paved the way for Mizoram’s statehood in 1987.
analogy: Two related agreements were signed in the same week, but by different parties and for different purposes; remember the main Accord as the month-end settlement.
traps: 25 June is the separate Congress–MNF agreement, not the Government of India–MNF Mizo Accord.
If a paper’s choices omit 30 June 1986, flag the item instead of scoring the closest date.
formulae: PYQ anchor: Excise Inspector 2021 GS-III Q67 — no correct date among the printed options.

subtopic: Traditional Mizo society, tribute and livelihood terms (PYQ review)
primer: Many Mizoram General Studies questions test specific Mizo terms for customary obligations, community institutions, festivals, tools and livelihoods. Learn each term with its function and context, and preserve the original spelling where possible. For example, the 2016 question on annual paddy tribute to the chief identifies Fathang. Avoid deriving a translation from a similar-looking word; local terms are not safely solved by English word roots.
analogy: Build a glossary card for each term: “word → who uses it → what it does → when/where it appears.” That is more reliable than memorizing a loose English gloss.
traps: Separate chief tribute from other customary dues and labour obligations.
Do not accept OCR-garbled spellings as reliable evidence.
For folktales, instruments, idioms and local games, require a trusted Mizo-language or academic reference before scoring.
formulae: PYQ anchor: Inspector of Taxes 2016 GS-III Q58 — Fathang, annual paddy tribute.
Use source review for uncertain spellings and oral-tradition variants.

subtopic: Mizo festivals and agricultural calendar (PYQ review)
primer: Chapchar Kut, Mim Kut and Pawl Kut are linked to different points in the traditional jhum and harvest cycle. Study each festival as a bundle—season or agricultural stage, customary activity, and characteristic observance—rather than as three interchangeable “harvest festivals.” Mizo calendar terms and festival dates may vary in transliteration and local description, so exact-language items need a reliable source.
analogy: Use a crop-year calendar: preparation, sowing/lean season, and harvest/storage are separate phases, and each festival belongs to its own phase.
traps: Do not interchange the three Kuts.
Do not infer a lunar-month name or a festival’s exact day from an English gloss alone.
Treat disputed oral-history explanations as traditions, not as universal literal facts.
formulae: PYQ anchors: Inspector of Taxes 2016 GS-III Q47–48; FCCAS Inspector 2019 GS-III questions on month names and customs.

subtopic: Mizo literature, oral tradition and historical attribution (PYQ review)
primer: Questions about the “first” Mizo writer, book, grammar, short story or folktale often depend on what counts: oral composition, transcription, a printed book, a school text, or a standardized script. Keep the milestone and definition together. T.H. Lewin documented Mizo-language material before the missionary-era primer; Lorrain and Savidge’s Roman-script work and educational publications belong to the 1890s. For author and folktale pairings, use a Mizo literary bibliography or scholarly source, not answer elimination alone.
analogy: A song’s creation, first written transcription, first printed edition and later standardized version are four different “firsts.”
traps: “First written down” is not the same as “first book printed in Mizo.”
Do not conflate a grammar/dictionary with a school primer.
Reject unsupported exact dates and names in low-confidence legacy answers.
formulae: PYQ anchors: FCCAS Inspector 2019 GS-III Q48, Q59 and Q75; Labour Officer 2021 GS-III folktale/literature items.
